content.text:
This confirms it precisely. Before commit 0dff56f, the code called `source.currentNode.getChildren(...)` and `source.currentNode.keySequence.iterator()` directly, evaluating `source.currentNode` fresh each time. Commit 0dff56f cached that value once into a local `sourceNode` variable at the top of the method, then reused the *stale* `sourceNode` reference in the branches that come after `source.moveDown()` mutates `source.currentNode` — a classic caching bug. The fix commit b1fbad5 reverts those two spots back to `source.currentNode` so the traversal picks up the updated node after moving down.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 0dff56fdb2525803c950b97fd6d2469357075703

## Reasoning
(1) I checked the git history of `PatriciaTreeMutable.java` around the fixed lines using `git log -S` for the introduced local variable `sourceNode`, and blame-style search on the pattern `sourceNode` in the file's history. This pointed to exactly one commit that introduced the `sourceNode` local variable and its use in the `reclaim` method: 0dff56f ("completely got rid of ExpirationChecker...").

(2) In that commit, the `reclaim` method was refactored to cache `source.currentNode` into a local variable `sourceNode` once at the start of the else-branch, replacing what previously were fresh reads of `source.currentNode` at each usage site. However, within the traversal loop, `source.moveDown()` is called, which mutates `source.currentNode` to point to a new node. The refactor left two usages (`sourceNode.getChildren(actItr.next())` and the reassignment of `srcItr`) still referring to the now-stale cached `sourceNode` instead of re-reading `source.currentNode`, causing the traversal to operate on the wrong (parent, pre-moveDown) node — the "weird reclaim bug".

(3) The bug-fixing commit b1fbad5 diff shows exactly these two lines reverted from `sourceNode.X` back to `source.currentNode.X`, matching precisely the lines that 0dff56f had changed from `source.currentNode.X` to `sourceNode.X`. This is a clean, unambiguous introduce/fix pair — no other commits touched these lines in between (confirmed via `git log --follow -p` on the file, where the only match to `sourceNode` in history besides the fix itself was 0dff56f).
